open_obligations: Note that Arnesen et al.'s debates are not recursive.
Check that the stability assumption could hold for reading comprehension questions.
Note the result gives no empirical evidence about LLM debaters.
in.other_title: Prover-estimator debate mitigates the obfuscated arguments problem in recursive debate
in.rationale: Arnesen et al. do not rule out that stronger models find judge-perplexing strategies such as obfuscated arguments. Brown-Cohen et al. propose prover-estimator debate, in which, under stability assumptions, an honest debater can win with a strategy requiring computational efficiency comparable to its opponent; it is a theoretical recursive protocol, not the QuALITY debate Arnesen et al. train.
in.scope: proposed ADDRESSES: whether a debate protocol can block judge-perplexing obfuscated strategies by stronger debaters, in complexity-theoretic recursive debate

text: Citing debate's mixed record in the literature, the authors say their results should be interpreted with caution and that they do not rule out that even stronger models might find strategies that perplex the judge and draw out debates, like the obfuscated arguments described by Barnes (2020).
title: Could stronger debaters find judge-perplexing strategies such as obfuscated arguments?
